title: The $A=4$ closure in the nuclear-physics literature: the Wigner $\mathrm{SU}(4)$ supermultiplet
html:
Remark (the A=4 closure in the nuclear-physics literature). The A=4 magic shell is the first Wigner \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet. The four single-nucleon spin-isospin states span the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}(4). Their totally antisymmetric product forms the one-dimensional singlet \Lambda^{4}(\mathbb{C}^{4}): the closed shell of {}^{4}\mathrm{He}. The vanishing dimension \dim \Lambda^{A}(\mathbb{C}^{4}) = 0 for A > 4 fixes the A = 4 locality of the closure.

Standard nuclear-mass systematics treat this closed-shell binding phenomenologically. The Wigner mass term vanishes identically at N = Z. It does not account for the anomalous extra binding of the even-even self-conjugate nuclei. A separate empirical cusp correction supplies that binding.

We locate this binding directly in the representation content of the nucleon braids. The T = 0 isoscalar channel — the self-conjugate partition (2,2) \vdash 4 — reproduces this scale with zero free parameters. The fully antisymmetric \Lambda^{4} channel acts as the closed-shell supermultiplet. The binding that nuclear phenomenology supplies through the Wigner term is here fixed by the \mathrm{SU}(4) structure of the A = 4 shell.
